scope: Whether a vendor-populated NVRAM cache lets the MD skip its NVRAM rebuild. Read-only diagnostics plus one explicit operator policy switch.

new_diagnostics.smem_cache: read-only, prints the NVRAM cache region AP/MD view, size and the first 64 bytes as hex
new_diagnostics.smem_clear: read-write policy for the first-start clear; accepts clear (default) or skip

observation_after_android_boot.sequence: boot the recovery image, let Android run ~44 s, then flash mainline and read smem_cache before any prepare
observation_after_android_boot.interpretation: non-zero and structured (offset/size-like pairs, e.g. 0x20, 0xa200, 0xa2c0, 0xae40, 0xb00, 0xb940, 0x332800), so the vendor stack does leave a populated cache behind

experiment.policy: smem_clear=skip, so the driver performed no first-start clear

result.cache_head_after: all zeros for the full 64 bytes

experiment.conclusion: the MD itself zeroes the NVRAM cache and rebuilds it from the file service at boot; preserving a vendor-populated cache changes nothing, so the first-start clear was never the deciding factor and the rebuild is not what keeps HS2 away

implication.vendor_timeline: the vendor reaches HS2 about 1.7 s after MD start, and its long NVRAM pass is a separate post-boot activity, so the ordering difference is real but is not explained by cache validity
implication.next_lever: the MD chooses to rebuild before HS2 regardless of cache content, which points at an AP-side input that decides the boot phase rather than at the cache

not_claimed: that the rebuild is required or unnecessary
